title: How To Handle Misbehavior The First Weeks Of School
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin frames early-year pushback from students as a normal test of whether a teacher is 'the real deal,' and argues that the central danger isn't student defiance itself but teachers panicking and abandoning their plan within the first two weeks. He describes in detail how caving to pushback teaches students that rules are negotiable, and contrasts this with the payoff of remaining calm and unmovable: students who initially resist eventually become the class's strongest allies once they see the teacher won't bend. The piece is written with unusual emotional intensity, casting persistence through early resistance as almost a moral test of character, and closing with a call to plant firm boundaries on day one and defend them without exception. Underlying the rhetoric is a concrete behavioral claim: consistent, patient follow-through during the toughest early weeks converts skeptical students into a class's biggest supporters.
points: Early pushback and boundary-testing in the first weeks of school is normal and should be expected, especially in challenging environments.
Caving to pushback within the first two weeks is identified as the single most common reason teachers lose control for the rest of the year.
Remaining calm, pleasant, and unmovable while reteaching the plan in greater detail turns skeptical students into a class's strongest supporters over time.
Students who resist hardest are described as secretly wanting firm limits, having learned distrust from adults who previously gave in to them.
quotes: They’re testing you. They want to know if you’re the real deal or just like all the rest.
Most teachers will panic and jump ship in the face of even semi-aggressive push-back.
One by one, as long as you remain calm and unmovable, your students will leap as if from a burning building onto your side.
They’ve been flattered and manipulated and told in not so many words that they’re weirdly different and don’t have the ability to control themselves.
But only if you persevere undaunted. Chicken out, give in, and be another spineless pushover and you’ll never know what they’re capable of.
